Understanding the project's data is split into three classes: original text and location, semantics and structure, and user records.

A LID addresses a position inside one material; another material can carry the same LID, so a citation must also know which material the position belongs to in order to resolve it into a meaningful passage.
Semantics and structure (concepts, relations, whole-book structure) build on the material and answer how to approach needed information; they support retrieval and reading planning.

Original-text position is a foundation running through the system: LID gives hierarchical, ordered positions so that build-side clues connect to the source and so that reading, citation, navigation and annotation share one addressing basis.

The cross-language contract is layered: language division (TypeScript for the build ecosystem, Rust for reading and runtime, Rust types generating TypeScript definitions), an interface made of frozen material artifacts written by the build side and loaded by the read side, and contract content covering both which fields and shapes exist and how the numbers are interpreted; cross-language work adds data-contract and debugging cost, and type generation solves only part of the consistency problem, so field meaning, units and version boundaries still need checking.

base-schema declares base types in Rust and exports TypeScript definitions through ts-rs (export_to ../../../packages/core/src/generated/), so LidNode.ts shows the corresponding fields and segment.ts imports the type to construct position nodes; the types named in the read passages are Span, LidNode and ReadOnlyBase, where ReadOnlyBase holds book_id, lid_nodes, graph_nodes and graph_edges and text must be loaded separately from the LID.

The Span Rust declaration carries derives [Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, TS, JsonSchema] with #[ts(export, export_to = "../../../packages/core/src/generated/")] and fields pub start: usize, pub end: usize.

Span's two integers mean a half-open interval of UTF-16 code units in the original text; generated Span.ts uses number on both sides, Rust's Book converts the text into Vec<u16> at load and text slices in the same unit; because build-side indices are JavaScript (UTF-16) while Rust strings are stored as UTF-8, indexing both representations with the same pair of numbers can yield different results.

base-schema answers where the types come from, not where the data lives: the base data (source.txt, base.json) holds the normative text plus book_id, lid_nodes, graph_nodes and graph_edges, and its authority and read entry points are ReadOnlyBase and Book::load.

critical_facts.text: ReadOnlyBase contains book_id, lid_nodes, graph_nodes and graph_edges; it stores identity and positions, not characters, and text is obtained only after the reading tool loads the passage so a LID resolves to the corresponding text.

LID is the shared locating basis for reading, citation, navigation and annotation; because another material can contain the same LID, a citation must also know which material, which is why book_id and lid_nodes sit together in the same base.

The relevant chapters group needed data into three classes: 原文与定位 (text and location - answers where the text is), 语义与结构 (semantics and structure - answers how to approach information), and 用户记录 (user records).

The cross-language contract covers two layers: field shape and type declarations, which type generation constrains, and field meaning/units/version boundaries, which source-level semantic convention must still constrain; agreeing on field shape alone does not prevent a unit mismatch, and parsing JSON successfully is not enough.

Span holds two integers start and end meaning a half-open range of UTF-16 code-unit indices in the original text; the generated Span.ts uses number, and Rust's Book converts the text to Vec<u16> and slices text by the same unit.

base-schema declares base types in Rust (Span, LidNode, ReadOnlyBase named) and exports TypeScript definitions via ts-rs to packages/core/src/generated; base data (source.txt, base.json) holds the canonical text plus book_id, lid_nodes, graph_nodes and graph_edges, with ReadOnlyBase and Book::load as authority and read entry.

The cross-language split is a deliberate interface choice (ADR-0021, 2026-06-22): TypeScript/Node for build-side parsing, deterministic text processing and harness orchestration, Rust for read-time/runtime; frozen artifacts make the seam mainly material delivery rather than frequent cross-language calls on mutable objects, and the cost is added data-contract and debugging work plus renewed checks of field meaning, units and version boundaries.

critical_examples.text: 教学字符串 A中B：中 在 UTF-16 下对应 [1,2)，在 UTF-8 字节序列中对应 [1,4)；把构建侧的 [1,2) 当作 UTF-8 字节范围只会取到该汉字编码的一部分，普通中文正文已足以触发这种单位错误。
Span 的 Rust 声明代码块：pub struct Span { pub start: usize, pub end: usize }，上方带 #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, TS, JsonSchema)] 与 export_to 注解。
讲解给出的判断题：用 LID 当 key 的原话缓存，在两份不同材料都含 LID 3.2.5 时会返回错的原文；key 需带上材料身份，且光改 key 仍省不掉正文加载这一步。

读者选区中的 Rust 函数：pub fn text(&self, lid: &str, end_lid: Option<&str>) -> Result<String, ToolError>；start 取 lid 节点的 span.start，end 在有 end_lid 时取该节点 span.end、否则取 lid 节点 span.end，最后 String::from_utf16_lossy(&self.source_u16[start..end])。

critical_facts.text: ReadOnlyBase 包含 book_id、lid_nodes、graph_nodes 和 graph_edges，不含任何正文字符；它存的是身份与位置，正文由读取工具加载后按 LID 找到对应文字。
LidNode 的 span 只指向原文范围而非文字本身；children 与 3.2.5 这类数值路径一起表达层级和顺序。
LID 只解决材料内部寻址：另一份材料也可以有同样的 LID，引用必须同时知道所在材料才能解析成有意义的原文，这正是 book_id 与 lid_nodes 并列的原因。
原文位置贯穿系统：LID 让构建侧整理的线索连回原文，也让读取、引用、导航和批注共用同一套定位依据。
理解项目所需数据分三类：原文与定位答「文字实际在哪里」，语义与结构答「怎样接近所需信息」，用户记录只被点名未展开。
base-schema 用 Rust 声明基座类型并通过 ts-rs 向构建侧导出 TypeScript 定义；生成的 LidNode.ts 能看到相应字段，segment.ts 导入该类型构造位置节点。
Span 含 start、end 两个整数，实际含义是原文中半开区间的 UTF-16 code unit 下标；构建侧用 JavaScript 字符串下标，Rust 字符串以 UTF-8 存储，用同一对数字直接索引两种表示可能取得不同结果。
数据契约分两层：生成类型约束「有哪些字段、用什么形状」，源码语义约定约束「这些数字怎样解释」；仅能成功解析 JSON 还不够。
共享语义固定为 UTF-16 code unit 半开区间：生成的 Span.ts 使用 number，Rust 的 Book 加载时把原文转成 Vec<u16>，text 按同一单位切片。
Span 的 Rust 声明带 derive(…, TS, …) 与 #[ts(export, export_to = "../../../packages/core/src/generated/")]，同一声明产出 TypeScript 类型。
base-schema 中被点名的类型有 Span、LidNode、ReadOnlyBase；阅读索引把这一组标为「基座定义、TS 投影」，回答材料的位置和字段怎样跨语言表达。
分工为 TypeScript 用构建生态、Rust 承接读取与运行时、由 Rust 类型生成 TypeScript 定义；代价是数据契约与调试成本，类型生成只解决部分一致性问题，还要检查字段含义、单位和版本边界。
主要交界面是已经形成的材料成果：构建侧写出数据，读取侧按约定加载；相比持续共享一组频繁变化的运行对象，方向明确的接口更容易说明各自责任。
2026-06-22 的 ADR-0021 在这条边界上选择 TypeScript/Node 预构建与 Rust 读时后端；冻结产物使跨语言接缝主要表现为材料交付，而不是一次采样中频繁互调两套可变对象。
base-schema 回答「类型从哪来」，不回答「数据放在哪」；基座数据（source.txt、base.json）装规范原文、book_id、lid_nodes、graph_nodes、graph_edges，权威与读取入口是 ReadOnlyBase 与 Book::load。
